title: The normalized constant-module class comparison is bijective
statement: Let A be a commutative ring and T a quasi-compact quasi-separated scheme. For every sheaf F of A-modules and n≥0, the class map of [def-asd-ordinary-finite-p1-kummer-class] from Hom_D(A_T,F[n]) to H^n(T,F underlying abelian sheaf), obtained by the forgetful Ext comparison and precomposition with the specified integral generator, is bijective. In particular the specified scalar Kummer class of O(1) has a unique derived module representative whenever the projective line is quasi-compact and quasi-separated.

proof.text: The constant-sheaf/global-sections adjunction identifies maps A_T→F with A-linear maps A→Γ(T,F). Evaluation at 1 is a bijection, with inverse a↦a x. Likewise integral constant-sheaf maps correspond to sections by evaluation at the integer 1. Expanding the specified integral generator makes these two evaluations equal.

proof.text: Apply the already proved adopted-library theorem AlgebraicGeometry.Etale.bijective_extToSheafHOf with this generator and the preceding degree-zero bijection. Its universal delta-functor comparison applies on a quasi-compact quasi-separated scheme in every degree. The displayed formula is exactly ordinaryFiniteClass after Ext.homEquiv.symm. Composition with this equivalence proves the claim. Surjectivity gives a representative of the fixed Kummer class; injectivity proves uniqueness of any representative satisfying the specified Chern predicate.
